correctness.rationale: For every missing translate, one strict facet inequality bounds its captured mass by an open facet halfspace. Every such halfspace threshold can be approximated by a translate aligned at a relative-interior facet point; the other finitely many facets have uniform positive slack s, and compact support within radius R ensures inclusion once t≥2R/s. Continuity from below proves the exact open-halfspace supremum including boundary atoms. Positive everywhere density gives a strict bounded-polytope versus halfspace inequality at any finite t. The actual standalone exact rational checker passed 1,480 empirical facet-witness tests in two through five dimensions and a non-axis-aligned triangle; computations do not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary paper establishes only pointwise asymptotic tangent-cone convergence under a boundary-null hypothesis (Theorem 5.2) and an arrangement method for empirical polytope depth (Section 7). Neither states or establishes the uniform finite cutoff over all query points for arbitrary compactly supported, potentially atomic laws. The earlier flag-halfspace literature discusses classical halfspace depth, not a finite exact dilation theorem for translated polytopes. Targeted searches of published mathematical findings, primary literature, and relevant prior claims identified no equivalent or stronger coverage. Priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: Upgrades large-dilation asymptotic convergence of an important convex-geometric depth operator to all-query exact equality after a computable finite scale for every polytope, without any atomless assumption. It reduces large-scale empirical polytope depth to finitely many 1D projection ranks. The Gaussian strictness separation identifies a mathematically real compact-support boundary, rather than a merely technical regularity condition. This is a structural geometric result, not a narrow parameter calculation.
